clue.text: Poet, novelist and critic providing wild parties after midnight

indicators.note: after places the parties behind the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its third letter, G
raves are wild all-night parties

explanation.surface: A literary all-rounder supplies riotous late-night parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read literally as the middle of 'night', its central letter G. Robert Graves was an English poet, novelist and critic; Graves is also a Bordeaux wine, one of the puzzle's theme of wines and cheeses.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves, author of I, Claudius, wrote poetry, novels and criticism.

clue.text: Swiss food man's consumed right before

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the letter goes inside the word for a man

parts.note: a guy is a man; the 's stands for has
ere is an old word meaning before

explanation.surface: A man ate some Swiss food, the correct one, earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruyère is a hard cheese from the Swiss canton of Fribourg.

clue.text: Fish that's found between rays

definitions.meaning: to fish with a rod and line
in geometry the figure between two rays from a point

explanation.surface: A sea creature living among skates and other rays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rays' suggests the flat fish; here it means lines radiating from one point.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line, and an angle is the opening between two rays meeting at a point.

clue.text: Rabble-rousing after leader goes for issue

indicators.note: the leader of the word is its first letter, which goes away

parts.note: sedition is speech or action stirring people against authority

explanation.surface: Agitation follows when the head of a group stands down.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one issue of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Dynasty brought to premature end? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: cutting something short before its end means dropping the final letter of the name

parts.note: the Romanovs were the last ruling dynasty of Russia

explanation.surface: A royal house cut off early, and the exclamation is a mocking 'bad luck!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' looks like British slang for bad luck, but the definition is literal: Romano is a hard Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Romano is a hard, salty Italian cheese, often grated like Parmesan.

clue.text: Where axes cut, for a start

definitions.meaning: the point where the x and y axes of a graph cross
a beginning or source of something

explanation.surface: Where the axemen chop, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' suggests choppers, but these are the axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin is the point where graph axes intersect, and also the beginning of something.

clue.text: For whom a spin to Saturn?

definitions.text: For whom a spin to Saturn?

indicators.note: spin means the letters whirl around into a new order

explanation.surface: Wondering who might take a trip to the ringed planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A and TO SATURN is itself a description: a space flier is the person for whom a jaunt to Saturn would be imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a space traveller, someone who might journey to another planet.

clue.text: Otherwise struggle in the direction of Umbrian town

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll be late'
to vie is to struggle or compete
to means towards, in the direction of

explanation.surface: Instructions to fight one's way to an Italian hill town.
explanation.walkthrough: Orvieto, a hilltop town in Umbria, also gives its name to a white wine, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Orvieto is a town in the Umbria region of central Italy.

clue.text: Kind of parties marginally represented here

definitions.text: Kind of parties marginally represented here

parts.words: Kind of parties marginally represented here
parts.note: a style of social gathering, and the theme of the answers around the grid's edges, which are drinks and dairy products

explanation.surface: A type of party only loosely present in this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marginally' means around the edges: the answers on the grid's perimeter are wines (Graves, Orvieto, Malaga, Alicant) and cheeses (Romano, Gruyère, Tilsit, Ricotta).
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering serving drinks and nibbles of cheese is a common kind of party.

clue.text: Dynasty celebrated in poetry

definitions.meaning: the ... (or Song) dynasty ruled China from 960 to 1279
a hero celebrated in verse is said to be ...

explanation.surface: A royal line praised by poets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sung is a Chinese dynasty, and also the past participle of sing, meaning praised in song or verse.

clue.text: One joins it in current local plan

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in places the joined pair inside the word for a local person

parts.note: a local is a native of a place

indicators.note: joins says the numeral is attached directly after the word it

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A local council scheme where someone joins in the electricity supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ITI (IT joined by I) inside NATIVE, after its N, and the current symbol I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An initiative is a new scheme or plan of action, as in a government initiative.

clue.text: Enemy confounded by one kind of Arab

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A foe is baffled by a particular Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' rearranges ENEMY into YEMEN, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native of Yemen, an Arab country in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Events one's enshrined in lyric poetry

indicators.note: being enshrined in something means being held within it

parts.note: epodes are lyric poems in which a long line is followed by a shorter one
one is I and the 's stands for is, so one's becomes I'S

explanation.surface: Happenings in which a person is honoured in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are incidents or events forming part of a longer sequence.

clue.text: Standing wave

definitions.meaning: standing as an adjective means lasting or fixed, like a standing order
a perm, a chemically set hair wave, is short for this word

explanation.surface: A stationary ripple, as physicists might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent means enduring or standing, and as a noun it is a long-lasting hair wave.

clue.text: Smart conversion securing energy from fuel, giving great performance

indicators.note: securing means the rearranged word holds the energy letter inside it
conversion means the letters of the word Smart are changed into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: from says the same energy letter is taken away out of the word fuel

explanation.surface: A clever change that saves energy from fuel makes for a high-powered performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' turns SMART into MASTR, which secures E to give MASTER; that E comes 'from' FUEL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Masterful describes skill of a high order, as shown by a superb performance.

clue.text: Inside house a lamp, primarily, provides overhead lighting

indicators.note: inside places the two picked letters within the abbreviation for house
primarily asks for the opening letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A lamp in the house is what gives light from the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhead lighting' suggests a ceiling fitting; it is the ring of light above a saint's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light shown above the head of a holy figure.

clue.text: What's more needed by prodigal son?

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking what more the wasteful son of the parable might require.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and what's more both add a further point to what has been said.

clue.text: Product of Spanish press that's not entirely factual, I can tell

indicators.note: not entirely says only a part of the words is used, a run within them

explanation.surface: Something in the Spanish newspapers is only half true, I can see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests newspapers but means a wine press: Alicant is a wine from the Alicante area of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicant is a red wine made from grapes pressed around Alicante in Spain.

clue.text: Sacred work religious leader put into moving pictures

indicators.note: put into places the religious leader inside the rearranged letters
moving means the letters of the word pictures are set in motion and rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A holy story told by a church leader in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving pictures' looks like cinema; 'moving' reshuffles PICTURES and R (from 'religious leader') goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Scripture is the sacred writing of a religion, such as the Bible.

clue.text: In Spain, fan targets one of their royals

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Spanish football supporter aims at a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese king, a royal princess.

clue.text: Ingredient of Italian desserts actor mixed with it

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer stirs something into an Italian pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' fits the kitchen surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian cheese used in desserts such as cannoli and cheesecake.

clue.text: Exhume ribs, among which other bones can be found

indicators.note: among which says the answer lies within the words just quoted

explanation.surface: Dig up some ribs and you will find further skeleton parts there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' is needed because ribs are bones too.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri, plural of humerus, are the long bones of the upper arm.

clue.text: Lacking confidence, son is advanced in easy job

indicators.note: advanced means moved forward, so the son's letter shifts nearer the front

parts.note: insecure means lacking self-confidence

explanation.surface: An unsure son gets promoted to a cushy post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is advanced' moves the S of INSECURE forward one place to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid position requiring little or no work.

clue.text: Provided backing when company merger is failure

indicators.note: backing means turning the word back to front

parts.note: if means provided, as in on condition that
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A business merger that goes ahead is a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merger' is a link word describing the joining of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a complete and humiliating failure.

clue.text: Kind of male found in Athens, originally

definitions.meaning: the dominant male of a group, the top dog
the first letter of the Greek name for Athens is the first Greek letter

explanation.surface: A dominant type of man discovered in the Greek capital, early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, and an alpha male is a dominant one.

clue.text: Hold between 55 and 56?

parts.note: a wrestling grip, read as a number: in cricket a Nelson is the score 111, and half of that is 55.5

explanation.surface: Asking for a wrestling grip located between two numbered clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson is cricket slang for a score of 111, thought unlucky; half of it lies between 55 and 56. The question mark marks the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A half nelson is a wrestling hold with one arm under the opponent's armpit and hand behind the neck.

clue.text: Get some help at home, in a way

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Hire a bit of domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a way or track for walking along.

clue.text: Wrongly list it in place of treaties

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters of list are not in their right order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has made a mistake listing the location of peace agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: The Treaties of Tilsit were signed by Napoleon with Russia and Prussia in 1807; Tilsit is also a cheese, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilsit, now Sovetsk in Russia, is the town where Napoleon signed two treaties in 1807.

clue.text: Port of Spain, wherein old woman and a young one returned

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman

indicators.note: returned means the pair of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a gal is a girl, a young woman

explanation.surface: A Spanish harbour where a mother and daughter came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the pair 'a young one' as a unit, not just the girl. Malaga is also a sweet fortified wine, fitting the puzzle's wine-and-cheese theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a major port city on Spain's Costa del Sol.
